basis: A saddle horse a visitor may ride, tied in each year near where the walk begins. The horse is the driven current26 horse with its own coat; its saddle, bridle and stirrups are generated by renderers/web/js/saddlery.js from the tack below and fitted to the horse's own skin. The patterns are the common riding tack of each period as general horse history describes it (a plain hunting-pattern saddle on a blanket with a crupper in 1812, the English hunting saddle on a square cloth in 1835, the English flat saddle on a felt numnah in 1904); no source places these horses, saddles or owners here, and nothing here is an identified animal or saddle.

rider.why: The visitor in the saddle is drawn as a period figure of the year (an anonymous stand-in, never a named townsperson), posed by renderers/web/js/rider-pose.js: seat in the saddle, feet in the irons, hands on the reins.

1812.pattern: plain hunting-pattern saddle on a folded wool blanket, crupper and iron stirrups; plain snaffle bridle without a noseband

1835.pattern: English hunting saddle on a square saddle cloth, iron stirrups; snaffle bridle with a cavesson noseband

1904.pattern: English flat saddle on a shaped white felt numnah, nickel stirrup irons, a breastplate; double bridle (bit and bridoon) with cavesson and browband

rows.name: Saddle horse
rows.basis: Reconstructed: no record places a saddle horse at this spot or names this horse. It is stood here so a visitor can ride in 1812; its tack is the year's period pattern (the file's basis).
rows.placement_basis: Stood a few steps ahead of where a visitor arrives (data/scenes/1812.json spawn), broadside with its near (mounting) side toward them; riding.js moves it to the nearest open ground if that spot is not clear.

fit.basis: Metres in the horse root frame. A rider sits his seat bones in the saddle's deepest point (the pelvis joint ~9 cm above the seat leather); the iron hangs a leather's length under its bar and is pushed out round the barrel by the rider's leg; the ball of the foot on the tread with the heel down puts the ankle joint above and behind the iron; the hands carried a little above and ahead of the withers, a hand's breadth apart.
